latest_rss.title: Journalist and #MeToo Activist Sophia Huang Xueqin Released From Prison After Five Years
latest_rss.summary:
Sophia Huang Xueqin, a journalist whose reporting on human rights and sexual abuse helped to galvanize China’s #MeToo movement, was scheduled to be released from prison last Friday, after completing a five-year sentence for allegedly “inciting subversion of state power.” Huang and her friend, labor activist Wang Jianbing, were detained in Guangzhou in September of 2021. After a long period of pre-trial detention, they were sentenced to prison in a secretive trial in 2024, and their appeals were denied.
Many of Huang’s friends and supporters, fellow journalists, and rights-defense advocates are concerned that even after her release, she may be kept under surveillance and have restrictions imposed on her freedom of speech and movement in a state of "non-release release." In the past, many released journalists and activists (including citizen journalist Zhang Zhan) have been subject to similar restrictions.

latest_rss.title: Putin Expands Federal Protective Service
latest_rss.summary:
Executive Summary:




The expansion of Russia’s Federal Protective Service’s (FSO) central apparatus by 12 percent since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine points to growing concern in the Kremlin over Putin’s personal security.



The repeated expansion of the president’s security apparatus reflects the regime’s growing distrust of other security structures and its perception of internal risks as real. This is turning the FSO into Putin’s personal “guard” and one of the centers of influence within the system.



In the long term, strengthening Putin’s inner security perimeter makes the Russian regime more fragile. The more resources it takes to protect one individual, the more clearly it signals the regime’s uncertainty about its own stability and the loyalty of the elites.

Russia’s September 18–20 State Duma elections have been described by some Russian commentators as a “special electoral operation,” echoing the Kremlin’s term for its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The increase in Russian hybrid warfare across Europe, from drone incursions to reckless maneuvers of combat ships, over recent months may make it necessary for Europe to take countermeasures.
